environmentVariables.description: The bucket. It must be private: this library decides who may be GIVEN a URL and has no say in who the object store will answer. `npx -p @filelayer/core filelayer doctor` reports whether yours serves unauthenticated reads.

environmentVariables.name: S3_REGION

environmentVariables.name: S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY

environmentVariables.description: How this agent names itself in the audit trail, recorded on every event these tools produce. It is what lets the chain separate "the partner opened this document" from "the partner's assistant opened this document".
environmentVariables.name: FILELAYER_MCP_AGENT_LABEL

environmentVariables.description: Set to exactly `true` to register delete_file. Off by default because deleting is not recoverable and an agent that misreads a sentence deletes the wrong thing silently.
environmentVariables.name: FILELAYER_MCP_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE

environmentVariables.description: Set to exactly `true` to register file_audit. Off by default because the trail is an organisation's whole history and a tool that returns it copies every file name, actor and denial into the model's context. Reading it is itself audited since 0.27.0, which was the previous reason; the default did not move.
environmentVariables.name: FILELAYER_MCP_EXPOSE_AUDIT

environmentVariables.description: Set to exactly `true` to register read_file. Off by default because a document returned by a tool is a document copied into a model's context; file_info plus a share link is usually what was actually needed.
environmentVariables.name: FILELAYER_MCP_RETURN_BYTES

environmentVariables.description: BigQuery: path to a service-account key file (Application Default Credentials). Required to use the bigquery engine.

environmentVariables.description: Snowflake: role to assume. Required to use the snowflake engine; has no default and must never be ACCOUNTADMIN (ACCOUNTADMIN, SECURITYADMIN and ORGADMIN are rejected before any Snowflake connection is opened - the check runs when the Snowflake configuration is first loaded, on the first Snowflake tool call; the server process itself starts regardless, so a bad role surfaces as a failed check_credentials or a tool error, not as a startup exit).
environmentVariables.name: SNOWFLAKE_ROLE

environmentVariables.description: Snowflake: secondary roles activated at login. NONE (default) means only SNOWFLAKE_ROLE is active in the session; ALL is the explicit opt-out that activates every role granted to SNOWFLAKE_USER.
environmentVariables.name: SNOWFLAKE_SECONDARY_ROLES

environmentVariables.description: Snowflake: path to an RSA private key file for key-pair auth (preferred over SNOWFLAKE_PASSWORD). Either this or SNOWFLAKE_PASSWORD is required to use the snowflake engine.
environmentVariables.name: SNOWFLAKE_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH

environmentVariables.description: Snowflake: passphrase for an encrypted SNOWFLAKE_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH key file, if the key is encrypted.
environmentVariables.name: SNOWFLAKE_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSPHRASE

environmentVariables.description: Snowflake: password (discouraged; prefer SNOWFLAKE_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH). Either this or SNOWFLAKE_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH is required to use the snowflake engine.
environmentVariables.name: SNOWFLAKE_PASSWORD

environmentVariables.description: Snowflake: account edition that sets the USD/credit price of estimates - standard (default), enterprise, business_critical or vps. The per-call edition argument can only raise it.
environmentVariables.name: SNOWFLAKE_EDITION

environmentVariables.description: Databricks: SQL warehouse server hostname (e.g. my-workspace.cloud.databricks.com, no scheme, no trailing slash). Required to use the databricks engine.
environmentVariables.name: DATABRICKS_SERVER_HOSTNAME

environmentVariables.description: Databricks: SQL warehouse HTTP path (from the warehouse's Connection Details tab, e.g. /sql/1.0/warehouses/<warehouse-id>). Required to use the databricks engine.
environmentVariables.name: DATABRICKS_HTTP_PATH

environmentVariables.description: Databricks: personal access token (simplest auth option). Either this or DATABRICKS_CLIENT_ID + DATABRICKS_CLIENT_SECRET is required to use the databricks engine.
environmentVariables.name: DATABRICKS_TOKEN

environmentVariables.description: Databricks: OAuth machine-to-machine service-principal client ID (preferred for automated use). Requires DATABRICKS_CLIENT_SECRET as well.
environmentVariables.name: DATABRICKS_CLIENT_ID

environmentVariables.description: Databricks: OAuth machine-to-machine service-principal client secret. Requires DATABRICKS_CLIENT_ID as well.
environmentVariables.name: DATABRICKS_CLIENT_SECRET

environmentVariables.description: Set to 1 to let estimate_query_cost/run_query_bounded accept text containing more than one SQL statement. Off by default: the cost cap is only known to cover the single statement the dry run/EXPLAIN priced. Skips only this server's scanner: Snowflake still rejects multi-statement text (sessions are pinned to MULTI_STATEMENT_COUNT=1), and only a single SELECT/WITH/VALUES statement is wrapped in a LIMIT subquery - a script runs unwrapped and its row cap (max_rows, default 1000) is enforced by the paged fetch.
environmentVariables.name: COST_GUARD_ALLOW_MULTI_STATEMENT_SQL

environmentVariables.description: Set to 1 (exactly that value) to let estimate_query_cost/run_query_bounded accept statements that are not reads. Off by default: only text whose first keyword (after comments and opening parentheses) is SELECT, WITH, VALUES, SHOW, DESCRIBE, DESC or EXPLAIN is estimated or run - a WITH must be followed by a SELECT or VALUES - because warehouse rows re-enter the model's context and can steer the next call. The gate is defence in depth: the authorisation boundary is the credential's grants (deploy a read-only principal). With COST_GUARD_ALLOW_MULTI_STATEMENT_SQL=1 every statement in the text must be a read, so BigQuery scripts (DECLARE/SET/BEGIN) need both opt-outs. Any other value leaves the gate on.
environmentVariables.name: COST_GUARD_ALLOW_WRITE_STATEMENTS

environmentVariables.description: Maximum number of run_query_bounded calls allowed in flight at once (positive integer, default 8). A cancelled call keeps its slot until its warehouse query completes or the 120 s watchdog fires; a call over the cap fails with a tool error naming this variable before any warehouse connection is opened.
environmentVariables.name: COST_GUARD_MAX_IN_FLIGHT_QUERIES

environmentVariables.description: Set to true (exactly that value) to let the read-only Databricks tools (check_credentials, estimate_query_cost) open a session on a SQL warehouse that is not RUNNING, which starts the warehouse and bills compute until it auto-stops. Off by default: the server first reads the warehouse's state through the Warehouses API (GET /api/2.0/sql/warehouses/<id>, CAN_VIEW/CAN_USE suffices) and, unless it is RUNNING - also when the state cannot be read - check_credentials returns ok=false and estimate_query_cost returns no byte or dollar figure, without opening a session. run_query_bounded is not gated: its own pre-execution estimate and the execution may start the warehouse. Any other value leaves the guard on.
environmentVariables.name: COST_GUARD_DATABRICKS_ALLOW_WAREHOUSE_START

environmentVariables.description: Set to true (exactly that value) to let the read-only Snowflake tools run SELECT CURRENT_REGION(), the INFORMATION_SCHEMA.QUERY_HISTORY read and check_credentials' session-context SELECT on a warehouse that is not STARTED, which can resume a suspended AUTO_RESUME warehouse and bill compute until it auto-suspends. Off by default: those statements are skipped unless the pinned warehouse's SHOW WAREHOUSES state is STARTED (also skipped when no warehouse is pinned or the state cannot be read), and the QUERY_HISTORY read is skipped whenever estimate_query_cost is called without a warehouse argument; estimate_query_cost then prices at Gen1 rates with the byte-tier heuristic and says so in a caveat, and check_credentials returns ok=true with a detail built from the SHOW WAREHOUSES row. USE WAREHOUSE, EXPLAIN USING JSON, SHOW WAREHOUSES and SELECT CURRENT_WAREHOUSE() always run; run_query_bounded is not gated. Any other value leaves the guard on.
environmentVariables.name: COST_GUARD_SNOWFLAKE_ALLOW_WAREHOUSE_RESUME

environmentVariables.description: Cap on running background jobs: decimal integer 1 to 8 (default 8). Blocking calls do not use this cap.

environmentVariables.description: Opt-in local usage log: on or off (default off). Records counts and settings, never prompts, code or paths; labels are caller text.

environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated allow-list of model slugs; anything else is refused. Unset: unrestricted. A single entry acts as the default model; an empty entry is a configuration error.
environmentVariables.name: CODEX_SUBAGENT_ALLOWED_MODELS

environmentVariables.description: Sandbox used when a call specifies none: read-only, workspace-write or danger-full-access. Defaults to read-only and cannot exceed the ceiling.
environmentVariables.name: CODEX_SUBAGENT_DEFAULT_SANDBOX

environmentVariables.description: Ceiling on what a delegation may do: read-only, workspace-write or danger-full-access. Defaults to workspace-write; danger-full-access must be set explicitly.
environmentVariables.name: CODEX_SUBAGENT_MAX_SANDBOX

environmentVariables.description: Ceiling on reasoning effort: none, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max or ultra. Unset: unrestricted. Higher efforts are lowered to a supported level, or refused if none fits.
environmentVariables.name: CODEX_SUBAGENT_MAX_EFFORT

environmentVariables.description: MCP servers from Codex's config a delegation keeps: none (default), all, or comma-separated names.
environmentVariables.name: CODEX_SUBAGENT_MCP_SERVERS

environmentVariables.description: Installed Codex plugins a delegation keeps: none (default), all, or comma-separated name@marketplace ids.
environmentVariables.name: CODEX_SUBAGENT_PLUGINS

environmentVariables.description: Whether a delegation keeps Codex's apps (connectors to external services): off (default) or on.
environmentVariables.name: CODEX_SUBAGENT_APPS

environmentVariables.description: Codex executable name or path. Unset: codex, searched on PATH. On Windows it must run directly, such as codex.exe; a .cmd or .bat shim is refused.

environmentVariables.name: DATA_DIR

environmentVariables.description: Preset name: english (default, bge-small-en-v1.5), english-fast, english-quality, multilingual, multilingual-quality, multilingual-ollama. Ignored when EMBEDDING_MODEL is set.
environmentVariables.name: EMBEDDING_PRESET

environmentVariables.description: Power-user override: any transformers.js checkpoint or Ollama model id. Takes precedence over EMBEDDING_PRESET. Switching auto-reindexes.
environmentVariables.name: EMBEDDING_MODEL

environmentVariables.description: Embedding backend. 'transformers' (local, default) or 'ollama' (requires a running Ollama server).
environmentVariables.name: EMBEDDING_PROVIDER

environmentVariables.description: Base URL of a local Ollama server. Only used when EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=ollama.
environmentVariables.name: OLLAMA_BASE_URL

environmentVariables.description: Override the embedding dimensionality when EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=ollama. If unset, the server probes the model on startup.
environmentVariables.name: OLLAMA_EMBEDDING_DIM

environmentVariables.description: Override Ollama's num_ctx for embed requests. Leave UNSET to let obsidian-brain auto-detect via `/api/show`'s `context_length` (e.g. nomic-embed-text=2048, bge-m3=8192, qwen3-embedding:0.6b=32 768). Setting this manually imposes a hard cap and may silently truncate longer inputs — see https://github.com/ollama/ollama/issues/14259. Ollama's own default is 2048 which truncates for any model trained on a larger context. See also https://github.com/ollama/ollama/issues/7008. Fallback when both env is unset AND /api/show is unreachable: 8192.
environmentVariables.name: OLLAMA_NUM_CTX

environmentVariables.description: Auto-pull the configured Ollama model when /api/show returns 404 (model not present). Default ON — choosing an Ollama-backed preset is implicit consent to download its model. Streams /api/pull progress to stderr. Set to '0' to disable auto-pull entirely (master kill-switch) and fall back to the actionable error path (`HTTP 404 — try: ollama pull <model>`).
environmentVariables.name: OBSIDIAN_BRAIN_OLLAMA_AUTO_PULL

environmentVariables.description: Opt-in to auto-pull for BYOM (custom EMBEDDING_MODEL) Ollama models OUTSIDE Ollama's official `library/` namespace. Default OFF — third-party models (e.g. `user/custom-fork`, `myregistry.com/team/model`) require this env var to be set to `1` before they will auto-pull, to prevent silent downloads of arbitrary user-named artifacts. Preset-known models (via EMBEDDING_PRESET) and bare model ids in the official library (e.g. `qwen3-embedding:0.6b`, `library/llama3:8b`) continue to auto-pull by default per the existing OBSIDIAN_BRAIN_OLLAMA_AUTO_PULL behavior.
environmentVariables.name: OBSIDIAN_BRAIN_OLLAMA_BYOM_AUTO_PULL

environmentVariables.description: Set to '1' to disable the live chokidar file watcher. Useful on SMB/NFS vaults where FSEvents/inotify don't fire reliably — fall back to running `obsidian-brain index` on a schedule (launchd/systemd).
environmentVariables.name: OBSIDIAN_BRAIN_NO_WATCH

environmentVariables.description: Set to '1' to skip the startup catchup reindex pass that picks up edits made while the server was down. The live file watcher still starts (via OBSIDIAN_BRAIN_NO_WATCH=1 to disable that separately), and first-time indexing on an empty DB is unaffected — this knob only governs the post-restart `enqueueBackgroundReindex` walk.
environmentVariables.name: OBSIDIAN_BRAIN_NO_CATCHUP

environmentVariables.description: Per-file reindex debounce for the live watcher, in milliseconds.
environmentVariables.name: OBSIDIAN_BRAIN_WATCH_DEBOUNCE_MS

environmentVariables.description: Graph-wide community-detection (Louvain) debounce for the live watcher, in milliseconds. Louvain is the only expensive op — batching it prevents per-edit CPU spikes.
environmentVariables.name: OBSIDIAN_BRAIN_COMMUNITY_DEBOUNCE_MS

environmentVariables.description: Per-tool-call timeout in milliseconds. Tools exceeding this return an MCP error instead of hanging.
environmentVariables.name: OBSIDIAN_BRAIN_TOOL_TIMEOUT_MS

environmentVariables.description: Override the adaptive chunk-size budget (in tokens). When set, this beats the capacity probed from the model's tokenizer or Ollama /api/show. Use for debugging or for models with stale tokenizer configs.
environmentVariables.name: OBSIDIAN_BRAIN_MAX_CHUNK_TOKENS

environmentVariables.description: Override the per-user config directory where obsidian-brain stores model overrides (`model-overrides.json`) and the user-fetched seed (`seed-models.json`). Default is `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/obsidian-brain` on macOS/Linux (or `~/.config/obsidian-brain`) and `%APPDATA%/obsidian-brain` on Windows. Both files survive `npm update obsidian-brain` because they live outside the package.
environmentVariables.name: OBSIDIAN_BRAIN_CONFIG_DIR

environmentVariables.description: Set to "1" to print a verbose synchronous startup trace to stderr — every preflight, createContext, server.connect, and shutdown step is logged with a monotonic timestamp. The LAST line before any silent failure tells you exactly which step the server reached. No-op when unset (no overhead). Use to diagnose silent-crash failure modes.
environmentVariables.name: OBSIDIAN_BRAIN_DEBUG

environmentVariables.description: Set to 'ndjson' for one-JSON-object-per-line stderr output (timestamp + level + message + structured fields). Default is human-readable plain text (`obsidian-brain: <message>`). Useful for piping logs into aggregators (Datadog, Loki, Vector, journald) that index structured fields.
environmentVariables.name: OBSIDIAN_BRAIN_LOG_FORMAT
